{{Short description|German-American neurobiologist (born 1958)}}
[[File:Günther_K.H._Zupanc.jpg|thumb|Günther K.H. Zupanc]]

'''Günther K.H. Zupanc''' (born 20 October 1958) is a German-American [[Neuroscientist|neurobiologist]], researcher, university teacher, book author, journal editor, and educational reformer. He is a Professor in the Department of Biology at [[Northeastern University]] in Boston, Massachusetts.

== Education ==
Günther Zupanc was born in [[Augsburg]] in (then) [[West-Germany]]. He graduated in Biology and Physics from the [[University of Regensburg]] (Germany) with degrees equivalent to Bachelor’s and master's degrees. He received his Ph.D. in Neurosciences from the [[University of California, San Diego]] (1990), and he was awarded the [[habilitation]] (Dr. rer. nat. habil.) in Animal Physiology from the [[University of Tübingen]] (Germany) (1995).<ref>{{cite web|title=Oxford University Press {{!}} Ancillary Resource Centre {{!}} Zupanc: Behavioral Neurobiology 3e - Author Biography|url=https://oup-arc.com/access/content/zupanc3e-student-resources/zupanc3e-author-biography?previousFilter=tag_about-the-author|website=www.oup.com|access-date=29 June 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Oxford University Press {{!}} Ancillary Resource Centre {{!}} Zupanc: Behavioral Neurobiology 3e - Günther K.H. Zupanc: Embrace the twists and turns, and never lose sight of your dreams|url=https://oup-arc.com/access/content/zupanc3e-student-resources/zupanc3e-author-narrative?previousFilter=tag_about-the-author|website=www.oup.com|access-date=29 June 2020}}</ref>

== Journalistic career ==
Before enrolling in college, Zupanc worked as a journalist for the [[Münchner Merkur]], a major daily newspaper in Munich, Germany, where he specialized in science writing. He also published numerous science articles in other newspapers and magazines. For one of his articles, he was awarded first prize in the contest ''Reporter der Wissenschaft'' as Germany’s best young science writer in 1980.<ref>{{cite news|title=Reporter der Wissenschaft|url=http://www.zeit.de/1980/21/reporter-der-wissenschaft|website=Die Zeit|access-date=2 November 2016|date=16 May 1980}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=I. Preis beim Wettbewerb "Reporter der Wissenschaft": Seine zweite Heimat heißt "Neritica"|url=http://www.zeit.de/1980/21/seine-zweite-heimat-heisst-neritica|website=Die Zeit|access-date=2 November 2016|date=16 May 1980 |last1=Zupanc |first1=Günther K. H. }}</ref>

== Academic career ==
Günther Zupanc was research assistant and research scientist at the [[Scripps Institution of Oceanography]] in La Jolla, California (1987–92), junior group leader at the [[Max Planck Institute for Developmental Biology]] in Tübingen, Germany (1992–97), senior lecturer (equivalent to associate professor) at the [[University of Manchester]], England (1997–2002), and professor at the International University Bremen (later called [[Jacobs University Bremen]]) (2002–09). Since 2009 he has been professor at [[Northeastern University]] in Boston, Massachusetts, where he also served as chair of the Department of Biology (2009–12). Zupanc was visiting professor at the [[University of Ottawa]], Canada (1994–97) and [[visiting scholar]] at the [[University of California, San Diego]], the [[University of Chicago]], the [[Max Planck Institute for Behavioral Physiology]], the [[Salk Institute for Biological Studies]], the [[Scripps Research Institute]], [[Tufts University]], [[Jacobs University Bremen]], and the [[University of Virginia]].

== Research ==
Zupanc has made important contributions to several disciplines within biology, including [[neuroethology]], [[neuroanatomy]], [[neuroendocrinology]], [[Developmental Neurobiology|developmental neurobiology]], and [[computational neuroscience]].

In his early work, he showed that seasonal changes in specific behavioral patterns are paralleled by pronounced alterations in the structure of brain neurons that control these behaviors.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Zupanc | first1 = G. K. H. | last2 = Heiligenberg | first2 = W.F. | year = 1989 | title = Sexual maturity-dependent changes in neuronal morphology in the prepacemaker nucleus of adult weakly electric knifefish, ''Eigenmannia'' | journal = The Journal of Neuroscience | volume = 9 | issue = 11 | pages = 3816–3827 | doi=10.1523/JNEUROSCI.09-11-03816.1989 | pmid = 2479726 | pmc = 6569919 | doi-access = free }}</ref>

His laboratory has extensively studied the behavior of weakly electric fish. Among others, these investigations led to the discovery of a novel behavioral pattern, the 'echo response'.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Zupanc | first1 = G. K. H. | last2 = Sîrbulescu | first2 = R.F. | last3 = Nichols | first3 = A. | last4 = Ilies | first4 = I.V. | year = 2006 | title = Electric interactions through chirping behavior in the weakly electric fish, ''Apteronotus leptorhynchus'' | journal = Journal of Comparative Physiology A | volume = 192 | issue = 2| pages = 159–173 | doi=10.1007/s00359-005-0058-5| pmid = 16247622 | s2cid = 1968690 }}</ref>

As part of his efforts to establish the [[brown ghost knifefish]] (''Apteronotus leptorhynchus'') as a powerful model organisms for the study of behavior and neural plasticity, his laboratory performed (in collaboration with the group of Jeffrey N. Agar of the Department of Chemistry and Chemical Biology at Northeastern University) a ''de novo'' assembly, annotation, and proteomics validation of the [[central nervous system]] transcriptome of this species.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Salisbury | first1 = G.J.P. | last2 =  Sîrbulescu | first2 = R.F. | last3 = Moran | first3 = B. | last4 = Auclair | first4 = J.R. | last5 = Zupanc | first5 = G. K. H. | last6 = Agar | first6 = J.N. | year = 2015 | title = The central nervous system transcriptome of the weakly electric brown ghost knifefish (''Apteronotus leptorhynchus''): ''de novo'' assembly, annotation, and proteomics validation | journal = BMC Genomics | volume = 16 | issue = 1 | pages = 166 | doi=10.1186/s12864-015-1354-2 | pmid = 25879418 | pmc = 4424500 | doi-access = free }}</ref>

Using the electric organ discharge of weakly electric fish as a neuroethological model system, Zupanc and his team were the first to employ a proteomics approach for large-scale identification of proteins involved in the development of a [[sexual dimorphism]] in behavior.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Zupanc | first1 = G. K. H. | last2 = Ilieş | first2 = I. | last3 = Sîrbulescu | first3 = R.F. | last4 = Zupanc | first4 = M.M. | year = 2014 | title = Large-scale identification of proteins involved in the development of a sexually dimorphic behavior | journal = Journal of Neurophysiology | volume = 111 | issue = 8| pages = 1646–1654 | doi=10.1152/jn.00750.2013 | pmid=24478160}}</ref> The results of this research have implications beyond this study, suggesting that astrocytes play an important role in the regulation of the activity of neural oscillators, including those that control a sexually dimorphic behavior.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Zupanc | first1 = G. K. H. | year = 2020 | title = Development of a sexual dimorphism in a central pattern generator driving a rhythmic behavior: the role of glia-mediated potassium buffering in the pacemaker nucleus of the weakly electric fish ''Apteronotus leptorhynchus'' | journal = Developmental Neurobiology | volume = 80 | issue = 1–2 | pages = 6–15 | doi=10.1002/dneu.22736 | pmid = 32090501| doi-access = free }}</ref>

In the field of neuroendocrinology, Zupanc and his collaborators succeeded in the cloning and pharmacological characterization of the first non-mammalian somatostatin neuropeptide receptor.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Zupanc | first1 = G. K. H. | last2 = Siehler | first2 = S. | last3 = Jones | first3 = E.M.C. | last4 = Seuwen | first4 = K. | last5 = Furuta | first5 = H. | last6 = Hoyer | first6 = D. | last7 = Yano | first7 = H. | year = 1999 | title = Molecular cloning and pharmacological characterization of a somatostatin receptor subtype in the gymnotiform fish ''Apteronotus albifrons'' | journal = General and Comparative Endocrinology | volume = 115 | issue = 3| pages = 333–345 | doi=10.1006/gcen.1999.7316| pmid = 10480984 }}</ref>

His laboratory developed a novel ''in vitro'' technique to trace neural connections in the brain.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Zupanc | first1 = G. K. H. | year = 1998 | title = An ''in vitro'' technique for tracing neuronal connections in the teleost brain | journal = Brain Research Protocols | volume = 3 | issue = 1 | pages = 37–51 | doi=10.1016/s1385-299x(98)00019-1| pmid = 9767097 }}</ref> This approach led to the discovery of numerous previously unknown connections in the brain of [[teleost fish]].

Since the early 1990s, Zupanc’s research group has pioneered the study of adult neurogenesis (the generation of new neurons in the adult central nervous system) in teleosts. He and his wife Marianne M. Zupanc introduced labeling of mitotic cells with 5-bromo-2'-deoxyuridine (BrdU) to research on adult neurogenesis.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Zupanc | first1 = G. K. H. | last2 = Zupanc | first2 = M.M. | year = 1992 | title = Birth and migration of neurons in the central posterior/prepacemaker nucleus during adulthood in weakly electric knifefish, ''Eigenmannia'' sp. | journal = Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America | volume = 89 | issue = 20| pages = 9539–9543 | doi=10.1073/pnas.89.20.9539| pmid = 1409663 | pmc = 50167 | bibcode = 1992PNAS...89.9539Z | doi-access = free }}</ref> Since then, this method has been used by numerous investigators working in this area. His research group performed the first complete mapping of proliferation zones in the adult brain of any vertebrate species (1995),<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Zupanc | first1 = G. K. H. | last2 = Horschke | first2 = I. | year = 1995 | title = Proliferation zones in the brain of adult gymnotiform fish: a quantitative mapping study | journal = The Journal of Comparative Neurology | volume = 353 | issue = 2| pages = 213–233 | doi=10.1002/cne.903530205| pmid = 7745132 | s2cid = 30403718 }}</ref> and he and his associates introduced zebrafish (2005)<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Zupanc | first1 = G. K. H. | last2 = Hinsch | first2 = K. | last3 = Gage | first3 = F.H. | year = 2005 | title = Proliferation, migration, neuronal differentiation, and long-term survival of new cells in the adult brain of zebrafish | journal = The Journal of Comparative Neurology | volume = 488 | issue = 3| pages = 290–319 | doi=10.1002/cne.20571| pmid = 15952170 | s2cid = 12522204 }}</ref> and tilapia (2012)<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Teles | first1 = M.C. | last2 = Sîrbulescu | first2 = R.F. | last3 = Wellbrock | first3 = U.M. | last4 = Oliveira | first4 = R.F. | last5 = Zupanc | first5 = G. K. H. | year = 2012 | title = Adult neurogenesis in the brain of the Mozambique Tilapia, ''Oreochromis mossambicus'' | journal = Journal of Comparative Physiology A | volume = 198 | issue = 6| pages = 427–449 | doi=10.1007/s00359-012-0721-6| pmid = 22491885 | hdl = 10400.12/7740 | s2cid = 10210760 | hdl-access = free }}</ref> as model systems to study adult neurogenesis. To provide an explanation for the biological function of adult neurogenesis, he formulated the 'matching hypothesis.' According to this hypothesis, neurogenesis in the adult central nervous system is the result of the continuous generation of new muscle fibers and sensory receptor cells in the periphery.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Zupanc | first1 = G. K. H. | year = 2001 | title = Adult neurogenesis and neuronal regeneration in teleost fish | journal = Brain, Behavior and Evolution | volume = 58 | issue = 5| pages = 250–275 | doi=10.1159/000057569| pmid = 11978945 | s2cid = 39958707 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Zupanc | first1 = G. K. H. | year = 2006 | title = Neurogenesis and neuronal regeneration in the adult fish brain | journal = Journal of Comparative Physiology A | volume = 192 | issue = 6| pages = 649–670 | doi=10.1007/s00359-006-0104-y| pmid = 16463148 | s2cid = 24063389 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Zupanc | first1 = G. K. H. | year = 2008 | title = Adult neurogenesis and neuronal regeneration in the brain of teleost fish | journal = Journal of Physiology, Paris | volume = 102 | issue = 4–6| pages = 357–373 | doi=10.1016/j.jphysparis.2008.10.007| pmid = 18984045 | s2cid = 24069980 }}</ref> To maintain a constant ratio between the peripheral motor and sensory elements on the one side, and the central elements on the other, any numerical change in the periphery prompts a corresponding numerical alteration (production or loss of neurons) in the central nervous system.

He and his team also demonstrated that the continued generation of new neurons in the adult central nervous system of teleost fish is closely linked to the enormous potential of this taxon to regenerate nervous tissue and to recover behavioral function after brain lesions and spinal cord injury.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Sîrbulescu | first1 = R.F. | last2 = Zupanc | first2 = G. K. H. | year = 2011 | title = Spinal cord repair in regeneration-competent vertebrates: adult teleost fish as a model system | journal = Brain Research Reviews | volume = 67 | issue = 1–2| pages = 73–93 | doi=10.1016/j.brainresrev.2010.11.001| pmid = 21059372 | s2cid = 28141774 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Zupanc | first1 = G. K. H. | last2 = Sîrbulescu | first2 = R.F. | year = 2011 | title = Adult neurogenesis and neuronal regeneration in the central nervous system of teleost fish | journal = European Journal of Neuroscience | volume = 34 | issue = 6| pages = 917–929 | doi=10.1111/j.1460-9568.2011.07854.x| pmid = 21929625 | s2cid = 23889436 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.northeastern.edu/news/stories/2011/04/fish_spinal_chord.html |title=Fish offer clues to spinal cord renewal &#124; Northeastern University News |access-date=2011-12-07 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110408085138/http://www.northeastern.edu/news/stories/2011/04/fish_spinal_chord.html |archive-date=2011-04-08 }}</ref> By employing a proteomics approach, Zupanc and his associates performed the first large-scale analysis in teleost fish of changes in global protein expression after brain trauma and spinal cord injury. As part of this effort, the team succeeded in the identification of a large number of proteins potentially involved in the regeneration of nervous tissue.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Zupanc | first1 = M.M. | last2 = Wellbrock | first2 = U.M. | last3 = Zupanc | first3 = G. K. H. | year = 2006 | title = Proteome analysis identifies novel protein candidates involved in regeneration of the cerebellum of teleost fish | journal = Proteomics | volume = 6 | issue = 2| pages = 677–696 | doi=10.1002/pmic.200500167 | pmid=16372261| s2cid = 15468763 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Ilieş | first1 = I. | last2 = Zupanc | first2 = M.M. | last3 = Zupanc | first3 = G. K. H. | year = 2012 | title = Proteome analysis reveals protein candidates involved in early stages of brain regeneration in teleost fish | journal = Neuroscience | volume = 219 | pages = 302–313 | doi=10.1016/j.neuroscience.2012.05.028 | pmid=22659563| s2cid = 6850599 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Sîrbulescu | first1 = R.F. | last2 = Ilieş | first2 = I. | last3 = Amelung | first3 = L. | last4 = Zupanc | first4 = G. K. H. | year = 2022 | title = Proteomic characterization of spontaneously regrowing spinal cord following injury in the teleost fish ''Apteronotus leptorhynchus'', a regeneration-competent vertebrate | journal = Journal of Comparative Physiology A | volume = 208 | issue = 5–6 | pages = 671–706 | doi=10.1007/s00359-022-01591-w | pmid=36445471 | s2cid = 254068160 }}</ref>

In an expansion of their research on adult neurogenesis, the laboratory of Zupanc discovered the first vertebrate organism that lacks any of the hallmarks of brain senescence common to humans and all mammalian species examined thus far.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Traniello | first1 = I.M. | last2 = Sîrbulescu | first2 = R.F. | last3 = Ilieş | first3 = I. | last4 = Zupanc | first4 = G. K. H. | year = 2014 | title = Age-related changes in stem cell dynamics, neurogenesis, apoptosis, and gliosis in the adult brain: a novel teleost fish model of negligible senescence | journal = Developmental Neurobiology | volume = 74 | issue = 5| pages = 514–530 | doi=10.1002/dneu.22145| pmid = 24293183 | s2cid = 24904520 }}</ref> In contrast to the latter, brown ghost knifefish (''Apteronotus leptorhynchus'') do not exhibit any significant age-related decline in stem/progenitor cell proliferation, neuronal and glial differentiation, or long-term survival of newly generated cells. The availability of this first vertebrate model of ‘negligible senescence’ provides unprecedented opportunities for a better understanding of the biology of aging and of the cellular mechanisms that protect brains from senescing.

As the first investigator in the field of adult neurogenesis, Zupanc and his laboratory succeeded in generating three-dimensional, high-resolution maps of adult stem cells and their progeny, as well as molecular profiles of these cells, in the spinal cord.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Sîrbulescu | first1 = R.F. | last2 = Ilieş | first2 = I. | last3 = Meyer | first3 = A. | last4 = Zupanc | first4 = G. K. H. | year = 2017 | title = Additive neurogenesis supported by multiple stem cell populations mediates adult spinal cord development: a spatiotemporal statistical mapping analysis in a teleost model of indeterminate growth | journal = Developmental Neurobiology | volume = 77 | issue = 11| pages = 1269–1307 | doi=10.1002/dneu.22511 | pmid = 28707354 | doi-access = free }}</ref> This work led to the development of a novel mapping approach (‘statistical mapping’), which enables researchers to produce global maps of central nervous system structures with cellular resolution. By integrating the big data set collected through such experimental work, Zupanc and his collaborators (notably Iulian Ilieş, Dávid Lehotzky, and Rifat Sipahi succeeded in building the first mathematical and computational models of stem-cell-driven tissue growth in the spinal cord during adult development and regeneration.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Ilieş | first1 = I. | last2 = Sipahi | first2 = R. | last3 = Zupanc | first3 = G. K. H. | year = 2017 | title = Growth of adult spinal cord in knifefish: development and parametrization of a distributed model | journal = Journal of Theoretical Biology | volume = 437 | pages = 101–114 | doi= 10.1016/j.jtbi.2017.10.012 | pmid = 29031516 | doi-access = free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Lehotzky | first1 = D. | last2 = Sipahi | first2 = R. | last3 = Zupanc | first3 = G. K. H. | year = 2021 | title = Cellular automata modeling suggests symmetric stem-cell division, cell death, and cell drift as key mechanisms driving adult spinal cord growth in teleost fish | journal = Journal of Theoretical Biology | volume = 509 | article-number = 110474 | doi=10.1016/j.jtbi.2020.110474| pmid = 32918922 | bibcode = 2021JThBi.50910474L | s2cid = 221643467 }}</ref> These models provide an important theoretical framework for better understanding tissue growth in the intact and regenerating central nervous system.

In collaboration with Rifat Sipahi, Zupanc also constructed computational models that simulate normal and tumorous tissue growth ''in vitro''.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Sipahi | first1 = R. | last2 = Zupanc | first2 = G. K. H. | year = 2018 | title = Stochastic cellular automata model of neurosphere growth: roles of proliferative potential, contact inhibition, cell death, and phagocytosis | journal = Journal of Theoretical Biology | volume = 445 | pages = 151–165 | doi=10.1016/j.jtbi.2018.02.025 | pmid = 29477556 | bibcode = 2018JThBi.445..151S | doi-access = free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Zupanc | first1 = G. K. H. | last2 = Zupanc | first2 = F.B. | year = 2019 | title = Stochastic cellular automata model of tumorous neurosphere growth: roles of developmental maturity and cell death | journal = Journal of Theoretical Biology | volume = 467 | pages = 100–110 | doi=10.1016/j.jtbi.2019.01.028 | pmid = 30707973 | bibcode = 2019JThBi.467..100Z | s2cid = 73424886 | doi-access = free }}</ref> Using this approach, the team has provided a theoretical explanation for the seemingly paradoxical effect that in lymphoma and prostate cancer cell-death-inducing chemotherapy sometimes induces tumors, instead of suppressing them.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Castañón|first1=Laura|title=Researchers may have discovered why some tumors grow back aggressively after radiation, chemotherapy. | date = 25 February 2019 | journal =  MedicalExpress |url=https://medicalxpress.com/news/2019-02-tumors-aggressively-chemotherapy.html| access-date=28 June 2020}}</ref>

As a translational spin-off of the basic research carried out in the laboratory of Günther Zupanc, his group developed a novel in vivo assay for screening and characterizing water-soluble anesthetic compounds.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Eske | first1 = A.I. | last2 = Lehotzky | first2 = D. | year = 2023 | title = The effect of urethane and MS-222 anesthesia on the electric organ discharge of the weakly electric fish Apteronotus leptorhynchus | journal = Journal of Comparative Physiology A | volume = 209 | issue = 3 | pages = 437–457 | doi=10.1007/s00359-022-01606-6| pmid = 36799986 | s2cid = 256939672 }}</ref>

A characteristic feature of the research of Günther Zupanc is the application of a multidisciplinary approach — the techniques and concepts used in his investigations are taken from a wide range of disciplines, including molecular biology, cell biology, neuroanatomy, neurophysiology, computational neurosciences, behavioral neurobiology, analytical chemistry, biophysics, and mathematical modeling.

== Editor of journals ==

Zupanc was senior editor of the ''[[Journal of Zoology]]'' (2007–11). After 14 years of serving as associate editor of the ''[[Journal of Comparative Physiology A]]'', he became its editor-in-chief in 2022. In this capacity, he is only the fourth chief editor of this journal, which was founded in 1924 by the later Nobel laureate [[Karl von Frisch]]. He is also a member of the editorial boards of ''Regenerative Medicine'' and ''Developmental Neurobiology''. Zupanc has edited special issues of several scientific journals, including ''Adult Neurogenesis: A Comparative Approach'' for ''[[Brain, Behavior and Evolution]]'', ''Electric Fish: Model Systems for Neurobiology'' and ''Integrative and Comparative Neurobiology: Papers in Memoriam of Theodore H. Bullock (1915-2005)'' for ''[[Journal of Comparative Physiology A]]'', ''Towards a Comparative Understanding of Adult Neurogenesis'' (jointly with Luca Bonfanti and Ferdinando Rossi) for ''[[European Journal of Neuroscience]]'', ''Adult Neural Stem Cells in Development, Regeneration, and Aging'' (jointly with James Monaghan and David L. Stocum) for ''[[Developmental Neurobiology]]'', and ''Centennial Issue'' for ''[[Journal of Comparative Physiology A]]''.

== Book author ==

Günther K.H. Zupanc published his first book, ''Fische und ihr Verhalten'' (1982),<ref>Zupanc, G. K. H. "Fische und ihr Verhalten. Die Erforschung der geheimnisvollen Welt unter Wasser. Mit einem Geleitwort von Prof. Dr. Arthur Davis Hasler, vorm. Direktor des Laboratory of Limnology der Universität Wisconsin in Madison (USA). 182 pp., {{ISBN|3-923880-11-1}}. Tetra Verlag, Melle (1982)</ref> while he was still an undergraduate student. This book appeared subsequently in an English edition under the title ''Fish and Their Behavior''<ref>Zupanc, G. K. H. "Fish and Their Behavior. How Fishes Live - Specially Written for Aquarists. Preface by Dr. Dr. h.c. Dr. h.c. Arthur Davis Hasler, Professor Emeritus at the University of Wisconsin in Madison (U.S.A.). 187 pp. 2nd edition. {{ISBN|3-923880-19-7}}. Tetra-Press, Melle (1988)</ref> and became a bestseller. Zupanc is editor of  ''Praktische Verhaltensbiologie'' (1988),<ref>Zupanc, G. K. H. (Editor): Praktische Verhaltensbiologie. Mit Beiträgen von Helmut Altner, Wilhelm Beier, Christiane Buchholtz, Martin Dambach, Benno Darnhofer-Demar, Klaus Dumpert, Dierk Franck, Reinhard Gerecke, [[Hartmut Greven]], Volker Hahn, Ernst Kullmann, Jürg Lamprecht, Martin Lindauer, Hans Machemer, Ulrich Maschwitz, Marliese Müller, Rüdiger Schröpfer, Roland Sossinka und Günther K.H. Zupanc. Series: Pareys Studientexte 61. 274 pp. {{ISBN|3-489-62936-1}}. Verlag Paul Parey, Berlin/Hamburg (1988)</ref> a laboratory manual used widely in German-speaking countries in biology education. His book ''Behavioral Neurobiology: An Integrative Approach'' (2004; third edition: 2019)<ref>Zupanc, G. K. H. "Behavioral Neurobiology: An Integrative Approach. Foreword by Theodore H. Bullock. Third Edition. {{ISBN|978-0-19-873872-5}}. Oxford University Press, Oxford/New York (2019)</ref> is the most frequently adopted text in teaching behavioral neurobiology classes in the world. In a review by the journal ''Integrative and Comparative Biology'', it has been praised as “a milestone in the neuroethological literature”.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://academic.oup.com/icb/article/50/5/911/646425| journal=Integrative and Comparative Biology | date=November 2010 | volume=50 | issue=5 | pages=911–912 | doi=10.1093/icb/icq133 | last1=Ewert | first1=Jörg-Peter | title=Behavioral Neurobiology: An Integrative Approach, Second Edition. * Gunther K. H. Zupanc. | doi-access=free | url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Science policy and educational reforms ==

[[File:Svenja Schulze and Günther K.H. Zupanc.jpg|250px|thumb|left|Günther Zupanc with German minister [[Svenja Schulze]] in Berlin in 2015]]

[[File:Günther K.H. Zupanc and Chancellor Olaf Scholz.jpg|250px|thumb|left|Günther K.H. Zupanc (left) and [[Olaf Scholz]] (right), Chancellor of the Federal Republic of Germany, in the city hall of Bremen in 2024]]

Günther Zupanc was among the founding faculty of the International University Bremen (subsequently [[Jacobs University Bremen]]), a unique private international university that combines features of the European Higher Education systems with the U.S. American Higher Education system. He played a leading role in defining and establishing the biology degree program at this institution. In 2009, this program received the top ranking of all universities evaluated by the ''Center for Higher Education Development'' (CHE).<ref>{{cite web|title=Jacobs University - Inspiration is a Place|url=http://www.jacobs-university.de/node/524|website=www.jacobs-university.de|access-date=2 November 2016|archive-date=30 July 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100730035322/http://www.jacobs-university.de/node/524|url-status=dead}}</ref> 

Zupanc has published extensively on history of science,<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Zupanc | first1 = G. K. H. | last2 = Bullock | first2 = T.H. | year = 2006 | title = Walter Heiligenberg: the jamming avoidance response and beyond | journal = Journal of Comparative Physiology A | volume = 192 | issue = 6| pages = 561–572 | doi=10.1007/s00359-006-0098-5| pmid = 16645884 | s2cid = 6878060 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Zupanc | first1 = G. K. H. | year = 2006 | title = Theodore H. Bullock (1915-2005) Trailblazer in neurobiology | journal = Nature | volume = 439 | issue = 7074| page = 280 | doi=10.1038/439280a | pmid=16421559| doi-access = free | bibcode = 2006Natur.439..280Z }}</ref> as well as various science policy issues, including biology teaching,<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1111/j.1469-7998.2007.00400.x | volume=274 | issue=2 | title=Teaching zoology in the twenty-first century: old challenges and new opportunities | journal=Journal of Zoology | pages=105–106 | last1 = Zupanc | first1 = G. == Personal life ==
Günther K.H. Zupanc is married to Dr. Marianne M. Zupanc, a microbiologist and high school teacher, with whom he has three children, Frederick, Christina, and Daniel.
